records.supported_name_scope: Representative receiving river/system identity for the selected Crique Neptune approach, Sinnamary corridor, Courcibo branch, Petit-Saut reservoir passages and lower Sinnamary coastal setting; not a uniform scalar hydronym.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The original IGN map views cover every selected component. The mainstem begins on a west-side feeder leading through the named Crique Neptune corridor into the Sinnamary, then runs north through the river's eastern upper/middle corridor into the Petit-Saut reservoir. The western selected branch follows the Courcibo corridor and its inundated continuation into the same reservoir. Their selected junction is inside the reservoir, followed by the Petit-Saut dam/outlet and the lower Sinnamary to the coastal estuary beside Sinnamary town. Independent original ORSTOM/CNRS and IRD maps distinguish the named river and branch, while the original DEAL reservoir map corroborates the impounded geography. The short final modeled northward extension crosses mapped coastal vegetation east of the present west-curving estuary; representative-system correspondence is supported at ordinary corridor scale, without asserting that this extension is a surveyed natural mouth channel.
records.region: French Guiana, Crique Neptune and Sinnamary mainstem with selected Courcibo tributary, Petit-Saut reservoir and Sinnamary coastal estuary.
records.completion_scope: Both mainstem and both tributary features are geographically covered by original IGN France views, independently named ORSTOM/IRD cartography and the Petit-Saut reservoir map. The modeled coastal extension is explicitly distinguished from the west-curving natural estuary.

naming_scope_details.observed_branch_spelling_variant: Rivière Kourcibo in the IRD reservoir figure
naming_scope_details.selected_tributary_terminal: Internal reservoir junction with the selected Sinnamary arm
naming_scope_details.terminal_limit: Final modeled northward spur crosses mapped coastal vegetation east of the west-curving Sinnamary estuary. The actual selected endpoint setting is observed; the spur is not asserted to be a natural mouth channel.
component_scope_limits: Sinnamary is a representative receiving-system candidate. It is not assigned uniformly to Crique Neptune, its complete initial feeder, Courcibo, all reservoir arms, or the final rendered coastal extension.

The selected mainstem does not begin at the natural Sinnamary headwaters south of the selected route. Its hooked headward approach reaches the Crique Neptune corridor before joining the separately continuing Sinnamary. The complete initial feeder name remains null.

Courcibo is the spelling on the historical Hydrologie plate and the IRD basin overview. IRD's reservoir figure labels the same western arm Rivière Kourcibo. This observation does not independently establish formal registry equivalence or a legal name boundary.

The mainstem and tributary join within the modern Petit-Saut reservoir. Historical channel/confluence context and the present impoundment must be distinguished; no precise submerged-channel or shoreline alignment is asserted.

The actual selected terminal is a short northward modeled extension into the coastal vegetation belt, east of the mapped west-bending Sinnamary estuary. It is not silently extended or relocated to the source map's natural Atlantic entrance. This local terminal generalization does not create a missing source interval for the bounded representative-system finding.
No exact spring, mouth point, bank alignment, legal naming boundary, comprehensive tributary inventory, contemporary water level or whole-feature scalar name is established.

records.supported_name_scope: No single representative hydronym is established for the combined Vunta Creek, Fish Creek, Rat River and western Mackenzie-delta channel route. Mapped component names remain separate.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Original 1976 NLUIS cartography covers the complete selected corridor at ordinary generalized scale: the Vunta Creek/Fish Creek headward drainage joins Rat River, follows the Rat River valley to the western Mackenzie-delta margin, continues north through a narrow edge-of-delta watercourse, crosses a reach of West Channel, then takes the north-running watercourse labelled Nikoluk to the south shore of Shallow Bay. The selected object combines separately named tributary, river and delta-channel components. No whole-route name or unique representative river identity is established.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The selection combines several named creeks, Rat River and separate delta channels. No source establishes one whole-route name or unique representative river identity.
records.region: Northern Yukon and Northwest Territories, Richardson Mountains to the western Mackenzie delta and Shallow Bay.
records.completion_scope: Three original 1976 NLUIS maps cover the full selected headward, creek/river junction, Rat River valley, delta-edge connector, West Channel reach, Nikoluk channel and actual Shallow Bay outlet. Physical connection is established; modeled traversal direction is not asserted as current flow direction.

component_scope_limits: Vunta Creek and Fish Creek are separate headward components; their names are not replaced with Rat River.

The selected route joins Rat River downstream of its separate southwestern headward lake setting. Summit Lake, Twin Lakes, Ogilvie Lake and Long Lake are shown nearby but are not selected lake passages.
Rat River does not supply a scalar name for the subsequent Mackenzie-delta edge channel, West Channel segment or Nikoluk outlet.

The cartography supports physical corridor and junction correspondence, not a legal naming boundary, current discharge direction at every delta bifurcation or a uniform downstream river-name sequence.
No new compound Vunta–Fish–Rat–Nikoluk name is proposed or accepted.

records.supported_name_scope: The historical upper river component bears McNaughton River, while Joe Lake and McNaughton Lake retain separate lake identities. Unnamed eastern connectors and the eastern coastal channel remain unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected route includes Joe Lake and an upper McNaughton-labeled component, but later traverses unnamed eastern lake/stream corridors. Neither a nearby river label nor the separate western McNaughton mouth is used to fill the missing linkage. Kaleet River, Sherman Basin and Falcon Inlet remain distinct neighboring context.
records.region: Mainland Nunavut; Joe Lake–McNaughton Lake and eastern McLoughlin Bay setting.
records.completion_scope: All of the selected FID2517 corridor and its actual terminal area were examined in four acquired primary NLUIS originals. This completes a bounded research attempt, not full geographic correspondence. Full map-area availability is distinguished from unresolved material connections.
records.material_pending_reason: Two essential connections remain unresolved: the selected northeast/east-side inland detour into McNaughton Lake, and its north-lake/eastern-stream exit toward the selected eastern coastal channel. Existing maps show the surrounding water network but do not securely establish the complete selected joining sequence.

records.supported_name_scope: Kokolik River is supported as representative system identity. The separately named Iligluruk Creek headward component and Kasegaluk Lagoon receiving-waterbody identity are retained; no whole-feature scalar hydronym is assigned.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected opening follows Iligluruk Creek from the mountain/foothill headward setting into the Kokolik trunk, rather than tracing the full separate upstream Kokolik valley. It follows the Kokolik north and northeast, then west and northwest across the coastal plain into Kasegaluk Lagoon near Point Lay. Adjacent Epizetka, Kukpowruk and Utukok drainages are excluded.
records.region: North Slope Borough, northwestern Alaska; Iligluruk–Kokolik corridor and Point Lay/Kasegaluk Lagoon coast.

Private crops clarify original labels, tributary versus adjacent drainage distinctions and the lagoon name. No tests, geometry revalidation, full source dataset or product changes were performed.
